Ternopil New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Ternopilska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Ternopil was founded in 1540, with Jews among its first settlers, and a fortified synagogue was built here as early as 1640; many Jews escaped the Khmelnytsky massacres of the following decade, though others were murdered. The town became a major center of the Haskalah (Jewish Enlightenment) movement in Galicia in the early 19th century, home to the influential Haskalah figure Yosef Perl and several other notable Maskilim, alongside both traditionalist Misnagdim and various Hasidic groups. The community peaked at nearly 14,000 people (about 50 percent of the town) around 1890, sustaining an active Zionist and religious educational life into the interwar period, before a pogrom in July 1941 killed thousands within days of the German occupation, followed by ghettoization, mass deportation to Bełżec in 1942, and the ghetto's final liquidation in 1943, which killed around 3,000 more. This cemetery, which emerged in the 1840s, was partly demolished during WWII, according to local testimony, with its gravestones used for road construction.
